title: Swimming pool certificate
what: A short check-up, after which you get a certificate saying you can swim in a public pool.
why: Before going to a pool. Many pools require it for adults and children.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes if the tests are ready
tell_doctor: For a child: illnesses and allergies

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A worm test is often required, either a skin scraping or a stool test. Ask the pool and the clinic.

prepare.title: Requirements
prepare.text: Ask the pool what kind of certificate they need and how long it is valid.

bring: Your ID, or your child's document
Test results, if done in advance
steps: You see a general doctor, pediatrician or skin doctor
The doctor asks about your health
Examines your skin, especially your feet
If needed, sends you for a test
feel: If a scraping is taken, it is quick and painless
after: Give the certificate to the pool
Watch the expiry date. It is usually renewed after a few months

faq.q: Why does the pool ask for a certificate?
faq.a: To keep out skin diseases, fungus and worms. It protects everyone.

faq.q: Can I get the certificate without tests?
faq.a: It depends on the pool. Many require a worm test.

reminders.text: Pool certificate tomorrow. Check whether a worm test is needed and bring your ID.
